pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: mm: per-process reclaim These day, there are many platforms available in the embedded market and they are smarter than kernel which has very limited information about working set so they want to involve memory management more heavily like android's lowmemory killer and ashmem or recent many lowmemory notifier. One of the simple imagine scenario about userspace's intelligence is that platform can manage tasks as forground and background so it would be better to reclaim background's task pages for end-user's *responsibility* although it has frequent referenced pages. This patch adds new knob "reclaim under proc/<pid>/" so task manager can reclaim any target process anytime, anywhere. It could give another method to platform for using memory efficiently. It can avoid process killing for getting free memory, which was really terrible experience because I lost my best score of game I had ever after I switch the phone call while I enjoyed the game. Reclaim file-backed pages only. echo file > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim anonymous pages only. echo anon > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim all pages echo all > /proc/PID/reclaim BUG=chromium:973963 TEST=build 4.14 for x86 Change-Id: I60a7ab5cfd4b4e065b767dd53cdd23e456e919dd Signed-off-by: Tim Murray <timmurray@google.com> Signed-off-by: Minchan Kim <minchan@kernel.org> Signed-off-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1727258 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Geffon <bgeffon@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mm: perproc-reclaim: do not discarding file-backed pages With testing, I found sometime perproc-reclaim shows regression with more LMKD kill because LMKD still relies on the file-LRU size while perproc-reclaim could make the file-LRU smaller. This patch changes the policy of file-backed LRU shrinking. Instead of discarding pages of perprocess reclaim, just makes them easy-reclaimable pages, for instance, move active file pages to inactive, clear PG_referenced and pte access bits. With that, we could keep file-LRU bigger so that more change to hit in the cache while VM can shrink quickly when memory spike happens. BUG=chromium:973963 TEST=build/boot 4.14 Change-Id: If12f2f0c7a7f5ad95fc0d205e6ef26bff9eb787a Signed-off-by: Minchan Kim <minchan@google.com> Signed-off-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1727260 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Geffon <bgeffon@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mm: make perproc-recalim THP aware I got a report there is THP user with perproc reclaim. Thus, this patch adds THP page handling logic. It's almost same with MADV_FREE in that "let's do not split the THP page unless we are not sure because THP collapsing is never cheap". To achieve it, it splits the page only if we know there is only user for the page via page_mapcount check. cryptohome: Stop binding TPM 1.2 delegate to PCR0 There are some Chromebook models with buggy firmware that sometimes changes the PCR0 value to an unexpected value. Therefore disable the binding for now for everyone, until those buggy models reach EOL - otherwise the Chrome OS attestation and smart card login features will be broken when the PCR0 is wrong. This CL is, effectively, a revert of https://crrev.com/c/1065826, which introduced the PCR0 binding. readahead: Handle readahead() calls with length larger than 32 pages The readahead() syscall isn't fully honoring the provided |count| parameter despite the man page saying "...bytes are read up to the next page boundary greater than or equal to (offset+count)". Kernels prior to v4.10 are capping the count to 32 pages (128kb). The following commit, included in versions >= 4.10, changed it to the optimal hardware I/O size which appears to be 128 pages on Eve: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/9491ae4aade6814afcfa67f4eb3e3342c2b39750 Fixing this is necessary for preloading the ARCVM system image file which after the ARCVM boot can have up to 4460 contiguous pages in core. Note that this also improves the average Chrome OS boot time as reported over 5 runs by login-prompt-visible in bootstat_summary's output by 12% on Eve. Before this change: login-prompt-visible = [ 4060, 4320, 4090, 4090, 4230 ] After this change: login-prompt-visible = [ 3420, 3770, 3700, 3690, 3690 ] BUG=b:137810150 TEST=ChromeOS boots 12% faster on Eve TEST=grep Cached /proc/meminfo doesn't grow significantly Change-Id: I41dd114a0864b509466580998d4e0dd9e21db162 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1717075 Tested-by: Philippe Liard <pliard@google.com> Commit-Ready: Philippe Liard <pliard@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org>

network_WiFi_LinkMonitorFailure: don't fail upon lack of disconnect This test is testing to ensure (a) Shill's link monitor detects a link failure (e.g., failing ARP requests) within a certain timeout and (b) the rest of the stack (driver, wpa_supplicant) responds appropriately when Shill requests a WiFi Reattach() Reattach() is just a "Reassociation attempt": https://w1.fi/wpa_supplicant/devel/dbus.html#dbus_interface which traditionally resulted in a disconnect/reconnect, but is now widened such that some drivers support the reassociation attempt directly, and therefore do not yield any disconnect. See https://crbug.com/990012#c4 for some more information about this. Anyway, the result is the 'iw event' only shows the "connected" event, with no disconnect in the meantime. This was confirmed in a WiFi sniffer packet capture. Since this behavior doesn't really violate (b), we should loosen this restriction, and avoid failing the test just because we didn't see a disconnect. A Reassociation should be as good as a Deauth/Reassociation in terms of "un-sticking" the driver. BUG=chromium:990012 TEST=run it on veyron_minnie-kernelnext Change-Id: Iddc454cbfde00aa23e60de1cfdf9d956e79d2f9a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1737468 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Neeraj Poojary <npoojary@chromium.org>
